title: Claude Code skill turns Bath-to-Bristol into a pixel-art road fly-through for $5.76
summary: This skill has Claude route a trip, pull real buildings, land cover and elevation from OpenStreetMap, and generate pixel art for each region. It then checks its own screenshots and fixes gaps until you can scroll along the real road.
agent_role: Claude routes the trip, bakes map data, generates and cleans art, and runs layout and frame-sweep checks, re-rolling bad images. The user picks the detail level and budget after seeing a cost estimate.
outcome: The author reports that Bath to Bristol cost $5.76 for 32 pictures and Kyoto cost $0.72. Both runs passed the self-check across 627 and 345 frames, and 10-34% of pictures needed re-rolls in testing.

curation.rationale: An original creative workflow with concrete example runs, per-run costs, re-roll rates and a screenshot-based self-check, plus enough detail to reproduce it. The README includes a disclosed affiliate link, which is a minor concern.
